description:
Make `jit invariant check` compute enforcement drift from captured declarations through the same function the validation report uses, fail on an unloadable gate registry as the report does, and drop the drift computation's unloadable-gate case.

## Background

- `check_invariants` (`crates/jit/src/commands/invariant.rs:50-58`) calls the executor's `compute_drift_findings` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:1470-1504`), which loads rules and gates from disk and treats an unparseable `gates.toml` as an unloadable source.
- The report's drift pass (`collect_enforcement_drift_findings`, `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:576-605`) runs over captured declarations and always passes the gate registry as loaded; an unparseable `gates.toml` fails declaration loading there, so `jit validate` fails with an error naming the file.
- `enforcement_drift` (`crates/jit/src/validation/drift.rs:165`) takes each source as a `SourceState` (`:104-120`). Once no caller passes an unloadable gate registry, the gate arm of `resolve_binding` that handles it (`:219`), its rustdoc and its unit tests (`drift.rs:443,463`) are dead; the unloadable rule-set case stays.
- `test_check_reports_unloadable_gate_registry` (`crates/jit/tests/cli_item_validate/invariant_check_cli_tests.rs:198`) pins the tolerant behaviour; the unit tests at `invariant.rs:96-197` cover drift cases.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `check_invariants` obtains the repository's declarations once and computes `DriftFinding`s through the validation-layer drift function the report's drift pass calls; it no longer calls `compute_drift_findings`.
- [hard] REQ-02: An unparseable `gates.toml` makes `jit invariant check` fail with an error naming `.jit/gates.toml`; the rewritten CLI test asserts it and fails on today's code, which reports an unloadable-gate drift finding.
- [hard] REQ-03: The drift function takes the gate registry as loaded keys, the unloadable-gate arm and its tests no longer exist, and drift findings, the unloadable-rules case included, are otherwise unchanged; the other invariant tests pass unchanged.

## Decisions

- **D-01** — Steward ruling 2026-11-04: `jit invariant check` reads its declarations once through the existing lock-free storage loads, so a read-only command never waits on writers (`@/charter/D-22`); no lock-free image capture exists yet. The interim loads move onto the read driver's lock-free capture with the read-driver work, whose criteria retire them. Rejected: capturing through a mutation session, which waits behind writers.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: an unloadable gate registry is an error for `jit invariant check`, as it is for `jit validate`.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Invariant check computes drift from captured declarations
